source_metadata.title: Metformin and weight changes in non-diabetic older people with HIV (METFORAGING): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, pilot trial

atoms.canonical_statement: The prespecified secondary analysis evaluated metformin effects on body-weight trajectories and metabolic outcomes in non-diabetic, non-obese older people with HIV.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We evaluated the effects of metformin on weight trajectories and metabolic outcomes

atoms.canonical_statement: METFORAGING was a double-blind, randomized, parallel-group, placebo-controlled pilot trial conducted at a single HIV clinic in Madrid, Spain.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: double-blind, randomised, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, pilot trial

atoms.canonical_statement: The parent trial primary endpoint was change in DNA-methylation-based epigenetic biomarkers of biological ageing; this paper reports prespecified secondary and exploratory metabolic outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary endpoint was change in DNA methylation-based epigenetic biomarkers of biological ageing

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants were followed through week 144, comprising 96 weeks of study treatment followed by 48 weeks of post-treatment observational follow-up.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Participants were followed through week 144, including a 96-week intervention period

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligibility required age 50 years or older.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: eligible participants were PWH aged 50 years or older

population.label: People with HIV aged 50 years or older enrolled in METFORAGING

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligibility required stable antiretroviral therapy for at least 3 months before screening.

inclusion_criteria: Stable ART for >=3 months before screening

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants were randomized 1:1 to metformin or matched placebo using central computer allocation.

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants, investigators, and outcome assessors were masked to treatment assignment.

atoms.canonical_statement: Metformin was given orally at 850 mg once daily initially and increased to 850 mg twice daily after 4 weeks, for a 96-week treatment period.

exposures.details: Study treatment for 96 weeks; usual titration from once daily to twice daily after 4 weeks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: metformin 850 mg ... or matched placebo for 96 weeks

atoms.canonical_statement: Study visits occurred at baseline; weeks 4, 8, 24, 48, 72, and 96; and post-treatment weeks 120 and 144; body weight was measured at each visit and BMI was calculated.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Study visits occurred at baseline, week 4, week 8 ... and weeks 24, 48, 72, and 96

atoms.canonical_statement: Waist and hip circumferences were measured at baseline, week 96, and week 144, and fasting metabolic blood tests were obtained at baseline, week 96, and week 144.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: circumferences were measured ... at baseline, week 96, and week 144

atoms.canonical_statement: Serum GDF-15 was measured at baseline and weeks 48, 96, and 144 using an ELISA.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: GDF-15) levels were measured at baseline and at weeks 48, 96, and 144 using an ELISA

atoms.canonical_statement: Adverse events were assessed at each visit, graded using the Division of AIDS adverse-event table version 2.1, and adverse reactions were defined by possible, probable, or definite relation to metformin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Adverse events were assessed at each visit by clinical evaluation and laboratory testing

atoms.canonical_statement: A prespecified metabolic outcome was the between-group difference in mean body-weight change from baseline to week 96.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: between-group differences in mean change from baseline in body weight and BMI at week 96

concept.text: Change in body weight from baseline to week 96

outcome.measurement_method: Body weight measured on calibrated scales

concept.text: Change in BMI from baseline to week 96

atoms.canonical_statement: Body weight and BMI were additionally assessed at week 144 after treatment discontinuation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: with additional assessment at week 144 after treatment discontinuation

atoms.canonical_statement: Clinically relevant weight gain was defined categorically as an increase of at least 3% or at least 5%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: clinically relevant weight gain, defined categorically as an increase of 3% or more and 5% or more

atoms.canonical_statement: Additional metabolic outcomes included waist and hip circumference, fasting glucose, HbA1c, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, and lipid parameters.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Additional metabolic outcomes included changes in waist and hip circumference

atoms.canonical_statement: Serum GDF-15 was an exploratory biomarker outcome associated with metformin exposure and weight regulation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Serum GDF-15 was measured as an exploratory biomarker

atoms.canonical_statement: Adverse events were a safety outcome classified by severity and causality.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Adverse events were classified by severity and causality

atoms.canonical_statement: No formal sample-size calculation was performed; the pragmatic target was 60 randomized participants and metabolic analyses were considered hypothesis-generating.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: no formal sample size calculation was performed; the protocol specified a pragmatic target of 60 participants

atoms.canonical_statement: Metabolic efficacy analyses used the per-protocol population of participants remaining on assigned treatment through week 96; safety analyses included all participants receiving at least one study dose.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Analyses of metabolic efficacy outcomes ... were conducted in the per-protocol population

atoms.canonical_statement: Between-group changes in body weight and BMI from baseline to week 96 were estimated using linear regression.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Between-group differences in change from baseline to week 96 in body weight and BMI were estimated using linear regression models

atoms.canonical_statement: Longitudinal weight and BMI trajectories were assessed using linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts and fixed effects for treatment group, time, and treatment-by-time interaction.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts to account for within-participant correlation over time

atoms.canonical_statement: Secondary metabolic parameters were compared using ANCOVA with the corresponding baseline value as covariate and treatment group as factor.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: estimated using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), with the corresponding baseline value as covariate

atoms.canonical_statement: Prespecified exploratory correlations between changes in GDF-15 and body weight were assessed with Pearson correlation within each treatment group.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: assessed using Pearson’s correlation coefficient within each treatment group

atoms.canonical_statement: No missing-data imputation was performed; available-case analyses were used and statistical tests were two-sided with alpha 0.05.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: No imputation was performed for missing data; available-case analyses were used

atoms.canonical_statement: The funder and sponsor were reported to have no role in data collection, analysis, interpretation, report writing, or the decision to submit.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: had no role in the collection, data analysis, data interpretation, writing of the report

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that metformin attenuated progressive weight gain over 96 weeks in non-diabetic, non-obese older people with HIV receiving contemporary ART.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: metformin attenuated progressive weight gain over 96 weeks compared with placebo

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors interpreted the return of body weight toward baseline after stopping metformin as evidence that the weight effect was reversible and exposure-dependent.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: indicating that the observed effect was exposure-dependent and may require ongoing treatment

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors interpreted the metformin-specific inverse GDF-15/weight association as supporting a possible link between metformin-induced GDF-15 changes and weight regulation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: support a potential link between metformin-induced changes in GDF-15 and weight regulation

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that the favorable safety profile and observed weight effect support larger, adequately powered trials to confirm efficacy and durability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: supports further evaluation of metformin as a pragmatic, scalable approach to weight management in HIV care

atoms.canonical_statement: The small pilot sample reduced precision and limited assessment of treatment-effect heterogeneity and extensive multivariable adjustment.

atoms.canonical_statement: Because participants were predominantly White and non-obese, generalizability to people with HIV who have obesity or more diverse ethnic backgrounds is uncertain.

extraction_limitations: The uploaded PDF contains the 16-page accepted manuscript but not the supplementary material; values in Supplementary Figure 1 and Supplementary Tables S1-S2 were not independently extracted.

The parent trial primary epigenetic-age endpoint and detailed safety laboratory results are reported in a separate publication cited as reference 16; those data were not reconstructed from this paper.
Atoms marked needs_review were structurally and sufficiency validated by the supplied Pydantic workflow but have not undergone independent human source verification.

Figure-derived post-treatment categorical percentages were read from Figure 2 in the uploaded PDF and retained as reported; no effect sizes were calculated beyond values explicitly reported in the manuscript.
